This screen

Open the deck

Open in prototypeslides.html#open-deck

Show the deck exactly as its author built it, with its own controls, and Pipeup's one tag in the corner.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

Maya opens the deck her colleague sent. She wants to page through it first and comment second.

Content
  • The author's deck: slide 1 of 3 as a 16:9 sheet in the middle of the window, its title and points, its number "1 / 3" and its own controls under it: Previous, Next and the count.
  • The comment control in the corner, showing the comment mark: no open threads yet. On a deck it will count only this slide's threads.
  • Nothing of Pipeup's over the slide.
Components
Comment control cornerIcon buttonSlide
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Next and Previous, and ← and →, turn the deck: the slide fades out and the next fades in over --ds-motion-settle. Turning is never blocked by Pipeup, in comment mode too.
  • Pointing at the tag slides its shortcut out; clicking it opens the menu; ⇧⌥C turns comment mode on (pin-on-a-slide).
Requirements
  • FR-016 On a deck, Pipeup follows the deck's own controls and never blocks turning a slide, in comment mode too, and its control counts only the current slide's open threads.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-open-deck-1FR-016PassedGiven the deck opened, when the page renders, then slide 1 of 3 shows with the deck's own Previous, Next and count, and the only thing of Pipeup's is the tag in the corner.
  2. AC-open-deck-2FR-016PassedGiven comment mode on, when Maya presses Next, then slide 2 shows and comment mode is still on.

Drop a pin on a slide

Open in prototypeslides.html#pin-on-a-slide

Let Maya point at an exact spot on a slide and say what she thinks there.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

On slide 2 she wants the second bullet gone. The spot, not the words, is what she means.

Content
  • Slide 2 of 3 in comment mode: the tag filled, the slide outlined as the block under the pointer with its naming bar reading "Slide · Raise the deck before spring" (default).
  • After an Option-click on the slide (success): a pin at the spot, open, and the comment box beside the slide with "Cut the second bullet; it repeats the title." typed and Comment ready.
  • The tag reads nothing yet: the thread is not sent.
Stand-ins
  • The pin: the mock shows the mock draws it at the slide's top-right corner, on the slide's pin layer. Look: in the product its point is at the exact spot Maya Option-clicked, kept as a fraction of the slide's width and height, so it keeps its place when the slide is resized (cmp-pin).
Components
Comment card composingNaming barAvatar smButton link, primary, quietComment control cornerIcon button quietPinSlideText field
States
  • EmptyNot applicable
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Option-click on the slide drops a pin at the spot and opens the box at once; the slide's naming bar's Pin does the same at the slide's centre; on touch, Pin then a tap.
  • The box sits beside the slide, never over it; Enter sends, and the pin shows its number, 1 on this slide.
  • Esc cancels with Undo, as on a document; ← and → still turn the deck while the box is open, and a box left on a slide that turns stays with its slide.
Requirements
  • FR-017 A pin dropped on a slide belongs to that slide, keeps its position relative to the slide when it is resized, and is numbered among that slide's threads.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-pin-on-a-slide-1FR-017PassedGiven slide 2 in comment mode, when Maya Option-clicks the slide, then a pin appears on it, open, and the comment box opens beside the slide with the cursor in it.
  2. AC-pin-on-a-slide-2FR-017PassedGiven the box with words, when she presses Enter, then the pin reads 1 and the tag reads 1.

This screen

Turn to the next slide

Open in prototypeslides.html#turn-the-slide

Keep Maya's bearings as the deck turns: only the current slide's threads show, and the tag says where the rest are.

Persona at this step
MLMaya Lindqvist

She has two threads on slide 2 and presses Next to go on. She expects the pins to stay with slide 2, not to follow her.

Content
  • Slide 3 of 3, with no pins: the two threads belong to slide 2 and went with it.
  • The tag shows the comment mark with the small dot at its corner: no threads here, but threads on other slides. Its label reads "0 here · 2 on other slides".
  • Comment mode is still on.
Wording
  • {n} here · {m} on other slides the tag's label on a deck.
Components
Comment control cornerIcon buttonSlide
States
  • EmptyThe default state: no threads on this slide, the dot showing for the others.
  • LoadingNot applicable
  • ErrorNot applicable
Interactions
  • Turning the deck fades the leaving slide and its pins and cards out, and the arriving slide and its own in, over --ds-motion-settle.
  • A comment being written on a slide that turns stays with its slide, words kept, and comes back when the slide does.
  • The tag's count is this slide's; the dot shows while any other slide has open threads.
Requirements
  • FR-018 Only the current slide's threads show; the control counts them, and a mark on it with its label say how many threads other slides hold.
Acceptance criteria
  1. AC-turn-the-slide-1FR-018PassedGiven two threads on slide 2, when Maya presses Next, then slide 3 shows no pin and no card, and the tag shows its mark with the label "0 here · 2 on other slides".
  2. AC-turn-the-slide-2FR-018PassedGiven slide 3, when she presses Previous, then slide 2's two pins and cards are back and the tag reads 2.

MLMaya Lindqvist

Before copying, Maya wants to see all her comments together; the deck shows only one slide at a time.

Content
  • The panel beside the deck, which has refitted into the room left: its filters and Close, then the list in deck order with a heading per slide, "Slide 2 · 2 open" (marked as this slide) and "Slide 3 · 1 open", each slide's threads under it with the words or the pin each is about.
  • The second card open in place.
  • The footer the tag turned into.
Wording
  • Slide {n} · {m} open a group heading; the current slide's group is marked.

Prompt for this screen

This journey

Review a slide deck

Maya reviews an HTML slide deck: she drops pins on the slides, turns the deck with its own controls while only the current slide's threads show, and sees every comment grouped by slide.

Goal
Maya says what she thinks about each slide of a deck, pointing at exact spots, and keeps her bearings as the deck turns.
Trigger
A colleague sends her a deck for tomorrow's talk and asks what to change.
Outcome
Her pins sit on the slides they belong to, the tag says how many threads are here and elsewhere, and the copied Markdown says which slide each one is on.
Success
A pin lands on the slide it was dropped on and stays there as the deck turns (FR-016). Turning slides is never blocked by Pipeup, in comment mode too.
